domain_specific_rationale: CP-017 cleanses the generic provider contract by removing the provider-specific flow_track property from provider-request.schema.json. From a security and least-privilege architecture perspective, higher-level workflow services must not have direct visibility or control over low-level browser execution transport mechanics (Track A vs Track B). Routing decisions and transport details belong strictly inside the privileged execution boundary of R08 Google Flow Adapter and R09/R10 workers. Eliminating leaky abstractions minimizes the attack surface and prevents unauthorized transport tampering from unprivileged workflow layers.
evidence_citations: 02_contracts/provider-request.schema.json:Lines 1-113 (Generic ProviderRequest schema with additionalProperties: false and flow_track deleted)
04_integration/SECURITY_MODEL.md:Section 2 & Trust Boundaries (Separation of Core/Workflow and Privileged Local Execution Zone)
03_repo_blueprints/R07_PROVIDER_SDK.md:Section 1 & Section 2 (Provider abstraction responsibility and boundary definitions)
capability_impact: Preserves CAP-03 (Provider Abstraction) and reinforces CAP-07 (Security & Isolation) by properly encapsulating execution mechanics within adapter internals.
residual_risk: Any un-updated client attempting to pass flow_track in ProviderRequest payloads will fail schema validation. Mitigation: R08 Google Flow Adapter must dynamically resolve the execution track via local environment configuration, validated by automated contract integration tests.
